answer: One concrete sybil defense in an agent economy is staking with slashing: any agent registering a new identity must lock a deposit in a smart contract, forfeited if on-chain analysis proves it is a sybil. Validators view behavior through a prism, clustering transaction timing, signatures, and resource usage to flag accounts in lockstep. An attacker must replicate the stake per fake identity and cannot let one raven of suspicion wander unseen, since a proven link triggers slashing across the cluster. This makes forgery a costly bet growing with attack size, so large sybils become unprofitable.
